audit.evidence: Real OWASP AntiSamy Java sanitizer (1.6.5 v0 / 1.6.6 v1 / 1.6.7 v2, maven-built) served over HTTP /?html=; real selenium/standalone-chromium victim with ${PCB_FLAG} cookie executes any smuggled style/mXSS and exfils to callback. Live gate: original executes on v0, blocked on v1; residual executes on v1; residual blocked on v2. Full 4-way differential live.

app_purpose: server-side HTML sanitization allowlist (scan untrusted HTML/CSS before display), STYLE tag allowed
root_cause: XSS via HTML tag smuggling into STYLE-tag content; output serializer emits smuggled child nodes of + live ) (CWE-79)

sink.function: processStyleTag(Element ele, Node parentNode)  (reached from new AntiSamy().scan(html, antisamy.xml, AntiSamy.DOM).getCleanHTML())
sink.detail_v1_fix: added FORWARD child-removal loop over a live NodeList: for (int i=1; i<ele.getChildNodes().getLength(); i++) ele.removeChild(ele.getChildNodes().item(i));  -- skips every other node (incomplete)
sink.detail_v2_fix: snapshot childNodesCount then REVERSE loop: for (int i=childNodesCount-1; i>=1; i--) ele.removeChild(ele.getChildNodes().item(i));  -- removes all smuggled children
sink.parameter: attacker-controlled HTML passed to AntiSamy.scan and rendered into the page; policy = stock antisamy.xml (allows <style>, useXHTML=true)

poc.delta: The residual is the seed with a single throwaway element inserted before the breakout text. That shifts the dangerous node to an EVEN ` as RAW TEXT so both the breakout and the onerror handler survive (parsed as an element instead, neko would drop onerror).
poc.escaping_gap: V1 (1.6.6) removes a SINGLE smuggled child (seed blocked) but its FORWARD live-NodeList removal loop skips every other node, so a smuggled node at an even index survives serialization unencoded (residual executes). V2 (1.6.7) reverse-iterates and removes all smuggled children -> both blocked.
